Elaine — thanks for the log slice. I've kicked off a deeper log collection and am looking at the ingress throttling layer and our upstream queues now. Initial observations:
- We see sustained 429s from the token-bucket limiter on the load balancer for the FS org id.
- A subset of requests show repeated retries at intervals < 500ms that are compounding the queue.
- Some backend shards are reporting elevated CPU that correlates with increased sequence lengths (customer is using longer context windows).

Immediate mitigation I'm attempting now:
1) Temporarily bumping org quota for FastShop on a hotfix pool (5-10m window) while we stabilize.
2) Enabling stricter SDK client-side  exponential backoff guidance (recommend jittered base 500ms, cap 8s).
3) Redirecting a fraction of traffic to a lower-cost model variant to take pressure off large-context shards.

I'll update in 10m with whether the 5xx rate drops after the bump. If we need leadership sign-off for extended capacity, I'll loop in Rishi.

What we did (complete):

We recommend the following immediate guardrails for launches:
1) Pre-authorize a scoped hotfix capacity with clear cost/credit terms.
2) Enforce client-side exponential backoff and jitter as default.
3) Canary 5% of traffic for 10 minutes into a separate shard pool.

I'll remain on call and will circulate a short incident timeline + RCA starter within 3 business hours.
